approaches.name: mobile-phone market information and demand aggregation for pastoralists
approaches.description: Mobile apps and decision support systems deliver prices, weather, pasture and conflict data and aggregate producer demand for market decisions. Practices: Mobile-phone demand aggregation and livestock market information system; Mobile-phone livestock market information system; Integrated decision support system for value chains; two-way mobile apps gathering producer and market operator data; Mobile phone delivery of market, weather and conflict information.
approaches.why_innovative: New service: mobile-phone market aggregation and market information - cue: 'piloting' | category Technological; adoption apply; judged in 1 round(s); final check: digital core, in_use before 2019

evidence.text: A third set of activities to be supported includes the piloting of innovative market arrangements such as livestock auctions; the development of product standards, traceability, and certification systems; the use of mobile phones to aggregate demand and conduct other commercial transactions; and scaling up the Livestock Market Information System.

extra_evidence.text: A livestock market information system based on mobile-phone applications will improve access in PAP areas to timely and reliable information for decision making, such as prices for different agricultural commodities in nearby markets.
Rather than developing a brand-new system, the project will scale up livestock market information systems that have been launched by other projects.

In particular, an integrated decision support system could provide access to the following key information: prices of major commodities in nearby markets, condition of pastures, water points, nearby markets, and conflicts.

This system could also enable aggregation of produce (through geo-location and uploading of information on produce that needs to be sold) and enhance the ability of rural producers to market their products.
An integrated decision support system will be piloted under this effort to remove bottlenecks in value chains; it could be scaled up based on the results of the pilot.
The marketing and rangeland information system will also have mobile apps to gather information from wider numbers of producers and market operators and will have two-way information flows.
Innovative pilots will deliver improved information (market, weather, and conflict) through mobile phones and contribute to improved decision making.

category.rationale: Technological: mobile channel and market information system are the mechanism

sector.rationale: Demand aggregation and market information serve livestock commercialization.

adoption.rationale: Digital core: mobile phones + LMIS | Innovative: pilot market arrangements | Category: Technological

approaches.innovation_basis: New service: mobile-phone market aggregation and market information - cue: 'piloting'

approaches.name: digital rangeland monitoring and livestock traceability systems
approaches.description: Satellite, drone and GIS tools monitor rangelands and feed balance, while digital systems trace and certify livestock products. Practices: Integrated pastoral decision support system for rangeland and markets; Drone mapping of rangelands and remote-sensing rangeland monitoring; Mobile-phone integrated decision support system for pastoralists; Digital traceability system for livestock products; Remote sensing for rangeland and feed balance monitoring; PAP livelihoods decision support information system linked to web-based MIS; NDVI/biomass satellite index for rangeland impact monitoring; GIS-based rangeland and pasture monitoring system from satellite imagery; Digital traceability and certification systems for livestock products; Drone mapping of rangelands and grazing units; satellite imagery biomass estimation for rangeland monitoring; satellite imagery and biomass tools for rangeland impact monitoring; digitized resource maps and pictographic rangeland plan tracking; geo-spatial platform with drone imagery of rangeland improvements; Remote sensing rangeland monitoring for management decisions; Animal identification and traceability system for livestock exports.
approaches.why_innovative: New service: integrated pastoral decision support system - cue: 'pilot' | category Technological; adoption apply; judged in 2 round(s); context expanded; final check: digital core, rare_or_absent before 2019

evidence.text: In addition, Subcomponent 3.3 will introduce digital technologies and pilot other innovations to solve critical bottlenecks in PAP value chains.

extra_evidence.text: Such technologies could include, for example, an integrated pastoral decision support system (rainfall, pasture, water availability, market price, conflict early warning etc.), certification and traceability systems for livestock products, and geo-spatial monitoring, among others.

Examples include the development of an integrated decision support system that relies on mobile phones, use of drones to map rangelands, deploying technology for improving traceability of livestock products to assess the potential for scaling them up across the project geography.
Rangeland performance will be monitored through remote sensing.
The project has set aside resources to pilot digital solutions.

In line with the project’s main objective of supporting resilient PAP livelihoods, it will provide specific technical assistance through the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO) and other agencies (such as specialized service providers and academic and research institutions), to support capacity building in specific activities, including remote sensing for monitoring rangelands and feed balance, new technology and innovations in feed and fodder production and processing, and PAP field schools.
(3) set up a PAP livelihoods decision support information system;

It assesses the Rangeland impact of the project Baseline,PY MIS, GIS and Special Project area with increased NDVI/Biomass Monitoring FPCU and RPCUs supported sustainable 4 and PY6 Survey Index corrected for weather variability Information landscape management System practices in the targeted range lands.
The indicator will consider the changes related to weather variability to specifically measure the changes attributed to the project investments.
Assesses the percentage of areas under project interventions, showing improvement in vegetation cover with economically important and environmental friendly plant GIS, species.
For biophysical monitoring following international protocols, the project will establish a GIS-based rangeland and pasture monitoring system, based on the interpretation of satellite/aerial imagery.
The monitoring system will be a national-level database system, with technical support provided to the F-PCU by a specialized national and/or international service provider.
Imagery interpretation may be supplemented by regular (on the ground) data collection on rangeland health and other trends, including the traditional rangeland management system.
(2) rolling out product standards and traceability and certification systems;

The project will also pilot innovations to remove core bottlenecks related to production, processing, marketing, and business arrangements in PAP production systems and value chains (such as certification and traceability of livestock products, the use of drones to map rangelands and grazing units, piloting of livestock business incubators, and an integrated decision support system).
Evaluation Project level • Results framework • Midterm and project completion assessments • Thematic studies and audits • Satellite imagery for estimating biomass development 3.
More specifically, satellite imagery and biomass estimation tools and techniques will be employed to monitor the impact of rangeland management interventions.
(2) introducing digitized resource maps and pictographic information on the rangeland management plans and their implementation progress;
The project will overlay community-level monitoring processes and integrate them into the upgraded MIS.

(3) geo-spatial platforms embedding digitized maps, geo- tagged photographs of physical structures, and drone imagery (with special authorization from concerned authorities) of rangeland improvements.
Rangeland monitoring through remote sensing will enhance rangeland management.

These prospects could be enhanced by introducing a practical, affordable animal identification and traceability system. • Opportunities exist to expand rainfed, water conservation, and irrigated agriculture in the Lowlands to meet market demand.
